title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Building the past with avoir
explanation: Use a form of avoir plus a past participle to talk about completed past actions. Course 9 reviews this pattern before moving to verbs that use être.

title: Passé composé with être
subtitle: Movement verbs in the past
explanation: Some movement verbs use être instead of avoir in the passé composé. The course practises this with verbs such as aller, partir, arriver, and venir.

examples.fre: Je suis arrivé en France hier.

title: Agreement with être
subtitle: Adding e and s in the past
explanation: With passé composé verbs that use être, the past participle changes to match the person when needed. Add e for feminine forms and s for plural forms.

examples.fre: Marie et Sophie sont parties tôt

title: Inversion with être in the past
subtitle: Asking passé composé questions
explanation: To ask a direct question, invert the form of être and the subject. The past participle stays after them.

title: Negative passé composé with être
subtitle: Saying someone did not go, leave, or arrive
explanation: Put ne before the form of être and pas after it to make these past forms negative.

examples.eng: They haven't arrived. / They didn't arrive.

title: Dépenser
subtitle: Talking about spending money
explanation: Use dépenser for spending money. In the passé composé, use avoir + dépensé.

examples.fre: Combien as-tu dépensé? / Combien avez-vous dépensé?

examples.eng: They have spent two hundred euros.
examples.fre: Ils ont dépensé deux cents euros.

examples.eng: I spent too much money yesterday

title: Comprendre
subtitle: Saying you understand
explanation: Use comprendre for 'to understand'. Course 9 practises it in the present and the past, including with object pronouns.

title: Ce que
subtitle: Saying what inside a sentence
explanation: Use ce que for 'what' when it appears inside a longer sentence rather than at the start of a direct question.

examples.eng: what (in the middle of a sentence)
I don't understand what you're doing
examples.fre: je ne comprends pas ce que tu fais

examples.eng: I don't know what I want.
examples.fre: Je ne sais pas ce que je veux.

title: Vouloir in the conditional
subtitle: Saying would like
explanation: Use voudrais, voudrait, voudrions, voudriez, or voudraient to say what someone would like. This is a useful polite pattern for requests.

examples.eng: I would like to go to France.
He would like to come with us.
Where would they like to go?

title: Passer + time
subtitle: Spending time or holidays
explanation: Use passer to talk about spending time somewhere or spending a holiday. The amount of time can follow passer directly.

examples.eng: I spent the holidays in France.
examples.fre: J'ai passé les vacances en France.

examples.eng: Pierre spent a week with Marie.
examples.fre: Pierre a passé une semaine avec Marie.

examples.eng: We spent two days in Paris.
examples.fre: Nous avons passé deux jours à Paris. / On a passé deux jours à Paris.

title: Combien de temps
subtitle: Asking how long
explanation: Use combien de temps to ask about a length of time. The same expression works with past, present, and other verb forms.

examples.eng: How long did you spend in France
examples.fre: Combien de temps as-tu / avez-vous passé en France

examples.eng: How much time would you like to spend abroad?
examples.fre: Combien de temps voudrais-tu / voudriez-vous passer à l'étranger?

examples.eng: How long has he been waiting here?
examples.fre: Depuis combien de temps attend-il ici?

title: Seulement
subtitle: Saying only
explanation: Use seulement to say 'only'. It can limit an amount, a length of time, or another part of the sentence.

examples.eng: I'm only spending two days here.
examples.fre: Je passe seulement deux jours ici.

title: Si seulement + imperfect
subtitle: Saying if only
explanation: Use si seulement with an imperfect form for wishes such as 'if only I could' or 'if only it were'.

examples.eng: If only I could finish it today.
examples.fre: Si seulement je pouvais le finir aujourd'hui.

examples.eng: If only we could see it.
examples.fre: Si seulement nous pouvions le voir. / Si seulement on pouvait le voir.

title: Espérer + infinitive
subtitle: Hoping to do something
explanation: Use espérer followed by an infinitive when the same person hopes to do an action.

examples.eng: I hope to go to France.
I hope to speak with Marie tomorrow.
I hope to leave at 8 o'clock this evening.
examples.fre: J'espère partir à vingt heures ce soir.

title: Espérer que
subtitle: Hoping that something happens
explanation: Use espérer que before a full idea with its own subject and verb.

examples.eng: We hope that Marie is doing well.
examples.fre: Nous espérons que Marie va bien. / On espère que Marie va bien.

title: Combien de + noun
subtitle: Asking how many or how much
explanation: Use combien de before a noun to ask how many or how much of something there is.

examples.eng: How many shoes do you have?
How many bottles of wine do you want:
examples.fre: Combien de bouteilles de vin veux-tu / voulez-vous?

title: Quel / quelle / quels / quelles
subtitle: Choosing the correct form of which
explanation: Quel changes to match the noun: quel, quelle, quels, or quelles. Use the matching form when asking 'which'.

examples.fre: Quel vin veux-tu? / Quel vin voulez-vous?
Quels as-tu essayé? / Quels avez-vous essayé?

title: Préférer
subtitle: Talking about preferences
explanation: Use préférer to say what you prefer. It can be followed by a noun or by an infinitive.

examples.fre: Quelle voiture préfères-tu? / Quelle voiture préférez-vous?

examples.eng: Do you prefer going to France or to Spain?
examples.fre: Préfères-tu aller en France ou en Espagne? / Préférez-vous aller en France ou en Espagne?

title: Devenir and revenir
subtitle: Become and come back in the past
explanation: Devenir and revenir are practised with être in the passé composé. Their past participles are devenu and revenu.

examples.eng: Pierre has become friends with Louis.
examples.fre: Pierre est devenu ami avec Louis.

title: Devoir
subtitle: Saying must or have to
explanation: Use devoir to say that someone must or has to do something. Follow the conjugated form with an infinitive.

examples.eng: We have to pay the bill.
What do you have to do?
examples.fre: Que dois-tu faire? / Que devez-vous faire?

title: Ne ... pas with devoir
subtitle: Saying must not
explanation: Put ne ... pas around devoir to say that someone must not do something.

examples.fre: Je ne dois pas partir tard.
Nous ne devons pas arriver trop tôt.
Il ne doit pas aller à Paris.

title: Ne pas avoir à
subtitle: Saying do not have to
explanation: Use ne pas avoir à + infinitive when something is not necessary. This is different from ne pas devoir, which means 'must not'.

examples.eng: I don't have to leave until tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je n'ai pas à partir jusqu'à demain.

examples.eng: You don't have to come with me.
examples.fre: Tu n'as pas à venir avec moi. / Vous n'avez pas à venir avec moi.

examples.eng: We don't have to go to the supermarket today.
examples.fre: Nous n'avons pas à aller au supermarché aujourd'hui.

title: Vouloir in the present
subtitle: Saying want and do not want
explanation: Use vouloir for what someone wants. Put ne ... pas around the verb to say what someone does not want.

examples.eng: I don't want to buy it; it's too expensive
examples.fre: Je ne veux pas l'acheter; c'est trop cher

examples.eng: What do you want to do?
examples.fre: Que veux-tu faire? / Que voulez-vous faire?

title: Pouvoir
subtitle: Saying can or be able to
explanation: Use pouvoir to say that someone can or is able to do something. Follow it with an infinitive.

title: Pouvoir questions and negatives
subtitle: Can, cannot, and can’t you?
explanation: Course 9 practises pouvoir in direct questions and negative questions as well as ordinary negative statements.

examples.fre: Ils ne peuvent pas le voir. / Elles ne peuvent pas le voir.
Ne peux-tu pas me voir? / Ne pouvez-vous pas me voir?

title: Savoir + infinitive
subtitle: Knowing how to do something
explanation: Use savoir + infinitive to say that someone knows how to do something, which can often be translated as 'can'.

examples.eng: I can speak English / (I know how to speak English)

examples.fre: Sais-tu parler anglais? / Savez-vous parler anglais?

examples.eng: Does he know how to speak German?

title: Imperfect carrier verbs
subtitle: Could, wanted, had to, and was going to
explanation: Course 9 uses imperfect forms such as pouvais, voulais, devais, and allais before an infinitive to build past ideas like 'could', 'wanted to', 'had to', and 'was going to'.

examples.eng: I was going to buy it.

title: Question words + imperfect inversion
subtitle: Asking what someone had to or wanted to do
explanation: Put a question word before an inverted imperfect form to ask about past plans, ability, wants, or obligations.

examples.eng: What did you have to do?
examples.fre: Que devais-tu faire? / Que deviez-vous faire?

examples.eng: How did you want to pay?
examples.fre: Comment voulais-tu payer? / Comment vouliez-vous payer?

examples.eng: Where were you going to stay tonight?
examples.fre: Où allais-tu rester ce soir? / Où alliez-vous rester ce soir?

title: On = one / we
subtitle: Using on for general people or for we
explanation: On can mean 'one' in a general statement, and it is also commonly used for 'we'. It takes a singular verb form.

title: On m'a dit / on dit
subtitle: Reporting what people say
explanation: Use on m'a dit que for 'I was told that' and on dit que for 'it is said that'. These patterns let you report information without naming the speaker.

examples.eng: I was told that Pierre was dead
examples.fre: on m'a dit que Pierre était mort

examples.eng: I've been told that the food here is fantastic.
examples.fre: On m'a dit que la nourriture ici est fantastique.

examples.eng: It is said that the streets are very beautiful here
examples.fre: On dit que les rues sont très belles ici

title: Question words + passé composé
subtitle: Asking detailed questions about completed actions
explanation: Course 9 finishes with question words such as où, que, pourquoi, quand, and combien combined with passé composé forms.

examples.fre: Où as-tu mangé? / Où avez-vous mangé?

examples.eng: What did you take with you yesterday?
examples.fre: Qu'as-tu pris avec toi hier? / Qu'avez-vous pris avec vous hier?
